3.1.content:
Google is implementing a Silicon Customer Owned Tooling supply chain solution to establish end-to-end visibility, traceability, planning, partner collaboration, and cost transparency across its silicon manufacturing network. The current landscape requires a clearer AS-IS baseline across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open, including core foundry and OSAT purchase order flows, material and supplier master data, batch and genealogy traceability, subcontracting settlement, enterprise structure, and existing partner data exchanges.

Business drivers for this engagement are the time-bound launch milestones for manufacturing visibility before Thanksgiving 2026, TSMC PO capability by December 4, 2026, technical go-live in January 2027, and business go-live in April 2027. The program also addresses current gaps in integrated planning, partner connectivity, organizational model readiness for the Silicon BU, and scalable supply chain execution as scope expands through Phase 3.

3.2.content:
- Establish the current-state baseline for silicon supply chain processes, data, integrations, and organizational structure.
- Finalize the target-state design for the Google Silicon COT operating model across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open.
- Enable constrained supply planning, inventory planning, traceability, and partner collaboration for foundry and OSAT operations.
- Configure SAP PP/MM and Kinaxis capabilities required for silicon manufacturing and planning.
- Integrate Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open to support planning, procurement, execution, and visibility.
- Deliver manufacturing visibility and TSMC MVP milestones in line with the phased rollout plan.
- Support user adoption through organizational change management, training, and reporting.

3.3.content:
The target-state process connects planning, procurement, manufacturing execution visibility, partner collaboration, and downstream financial and operational reporting across Google and its external manufacturing partners. Kinaxis will drive silicon planning and constraint-based decision support; SAP S/4HANA will manage core transactional execution, master data, material movements, traceability, and procurement processes; and E2Open will support collaboration and data exchange with TSMC and OSAT partners. The future state is intended to provide lot-level visibility, clearer ownership and handoff points, stronger batch genealogy, and integrated planning signals from demand through execution.

2.content:
This engagement covers the phased implementation of Google’s Silicon COT Supply Chain Process Implementation across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open to establish end-to-end manufacturing visibility, traceability, planning, partner collaboration, and cost transparency for Google’s direct operating model with TSMC and OSAT partners. The work will be delivered through a phased agile model from June 2026 through December 2027, with key milestones including Phase 1 manufacturing visibility before Thanksgiving 2026, TSMC MVP by December 4, 2026, technical go-live in January 2027, and business go-live in April 2027.

- Implement the core Silicon COT process across manufacturing, planning, procurement, finance, logistics, quality, and partner collaboration workstreams.
- Enable lot-level visibility, batch traceability, constrained supply planning, and yield-aware decision-making across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open, and required integrations.
- Deliver phased deployment, organizational change management, and user adoption support to stabilize operations and scale scope through Phase 3.

Deferred decisions, scope assumptions, and open design items are identified in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

4.1.content: Geographical scope covers Google’s silicon COT supply chain operations delivered across the United States, India, and Taiwan. Phase 1 and Phase 2 are limited to Taiwan manufacturing flows across TSMC, KYEC, SPIL, Google Hub, and warehouse locations supporting the initial COT operating model. Phase 3 expands scope to additional partner and logistics flows, including downstream movement involving Google USA, Foxconn, and Quanta, in line with the approved phased rollout.

4.2.content: Process scope includes Customer Owned Tooling supply chain processes required to establish end-to-end visibility, planning, execution, and traceability for Google’s silicon manufacturing network. In-scope processes include material master enablement, wafer and substrate procurement, TSMC inventory purchase order processing, OSAT subcontracting purchase orders, constrained supply planning with yield, inventory planning, production planning, materials management, batch traceability, lot genealogy, manufacturing visibility, partner commits and recommits, ASN and shipment visibility, and user adoption activities required to support business readiness. Phase 1 and Phase 2 process scope is limited to Taiwan-based manufacturing steps, with international mid-stream flows addressed in Phase 3.

4.3.content: Technical scope includes solution design, configuration, and delivery across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open for the silicon COT operating model. In scope are AS-IS assessment and requirements gathering for SAP S/4HANA and Kinaxis, target-state design finalization, SAP PP and MM configuration, Kinaxis setup for supply, constraint, and inventory planning, and incremental integration enablement between SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open using Google’s existing integration framework where applicable. The solution includes support for inbound capacity and contract manufacturer data, batch and genealogy visibility, planning signal exchange, and partner collaboration flows for TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL. Net new manufacturing collaboration and Silicon Data Hub integrations are excluded from Bristlecone scope.

4.4.content:
Services scope includes program management, fit-gap analysis, to-be process design, solution configuration, build, business process design documentation, functional specifications for approved custom development, test planning and execution, unit testing, system integration testing, user acceptance testing support, regression testing, performance testing, data migration support, cutover planning and execution, hypercare, organizational change management, train-the-trainer enablement, end-user adoption tracking and reporting, and knowledge transfer to the support team.

<IMAGE id="2a4a0eb1f4a9"/>

4.5.content:
Application scope includes the following functional areas:
- **Kinaxis:** Supply Planning, Constraint Planning, Inventory Planning, Analytics and Reporting, and Data Integration.
- **SAP S/4HANA:** Production Planning (PP), Materials Management (MM), material master enablement, inventory and procurement execution, batch traceability, and lot genealogy support for silicon manufacturing processes.
- **E2Open:** Vendor collaboration, structured commits and recommits, OSAT WIP event visibility, ASN visibility, shipment collaboration, and planning feedback to integrated planning processes.

5.content:
The solution architecture uses Kinaxis as the planning layer, SAP S/4HANA as the system of transactional record for procurement, material movements, production and traceability, and E2Open as the collaboration channel for TSMC and OSAT partners. The design is intentionally loosely coupled for the MVP, with existing Google integration patterns leveraged where fit-for-purpose rather than rebuilt. Existing data templates will be adapted for silicon planning needs, and incremental delta interfaces will be implemented for additional inbound and outbound data flows required by the COT process.

<IMAGE id="72b8c9d44014"/>

The deployment model follows a phased agile approach across Explore, Build, and Deploy, aligned to Phase 1 manufacturing visibility, the TSMC PO milestone, January 2027 technical go-live, April 2027 business go-live, and Phase 3 scale-out through December 2027. Phases 1 and 2 are limited to Taiwan manufacturing flows across TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL, with broader mid-stream and expanded scope introduced in Phase 3.

Change governance will be controlled through baseline design finalization during discovery, formal review of architecture and integration impacts before build, and change control for any expansion to interfaces, partner onboarding sequence, process scope, or system boundary decisions. Google-owned areas, including CO/FICO-owned configuration and Google-managed middleware configuration, remain outside Bristlecone delivery scope unless later approved through change control. <TECH TEAM: confirm whether Google BigQuery should be shown as an in-scope architecture component in this section or treated as an adjacent Google-managed platform.>

6.1.content:
Google and Bristlecone will execute this engagement through a phased agile delivery model aligned to Explore, Build, and Deploy. Work will begin with AS-IS assessment, fit-gap validation, target-state process finalization, and integration/data design across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open. Build activities will then proceed in iterative waves covering configuration, incremental integration enablement, data loading and validation, testing, training, cutover preparation, and release readiness.

The rollout will follow three controlled phases: Phase 1 to establish manufacturing visibility and TSMC MVP readiness, Phase 2 to complete the initial end-to-end silicon planning and business go-live, and Phase 3 to scale scope, partner onboarding, and future procurement cycles. Project management, integration, governance, and organizational change management will run across all phases, with regular weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews to track milestones, dependencies, risks, and decisions. Role-based training, UAT support, regression testing, performance testing, cutover execution, hypercare, and knowledge transfer will be completed as part of release readiness and stabilization.

7.1.content:
Project governance will operate through a phased agile delivery model with weekly delivery reviews, milestone steering checkpoints, and formal escalation aligned to phase outcomes. Escalations will follow three levels: workstream leads for issue resolution within the delivery team; Program Manager and Google project leadership for cross-functional, timeline, or scope decisions; and executive sponsors for matters affecting milestone commitments, commercials, or critical business readiness. Risks, assumptions, dependencies, and decisions will be reviewed in each governance cycle, with any scope, schedule, or commercial impact routed through the Change Management Process.

- Delivery will follow a phased agile model from June 2026 through December 2027, with manufacturing visibility targeted before Thanksgiving 2026, TSMC PO capability by December 4, 2026, technical go-live in January 2027, and business go-live in April 2027.
- Phase 1 and Phase 2 manufacturing flows are limited to Taiwan; international mid-stream flows are excluded until Phase 3.

- Existing integration patterns and data templates will be leveraged where feasible, with only incremental delta interfaces included in scope following discovery validation.
- BOM explosion is assumed to remain owned by PLM, with existing GPN and BOM structures available for Kinaxis and SAP consumption before configuration begins.
- Google ownership of WIP begins after probe completion at TSMC; ownership transfer at goods receipt will apply where relevant, subject to Google confirmation.
- Key lot events will be tracked at value-add handoff points rather than at every shop-floor transaction.
- OSATs will be modeled as vendors with subcontract purchase orders and SAP inventory locations, using a common four-step routing construct across in-scope partners.
- Kinaxis, SAP S/4HANA, and E2Open will serve as the primary in-scope platforms for planning, execution, and partner collaboration for this engagement.
- Manufacturing collaboration and Silicon Data Hub net-new integrations are not included in this SOW unless added through the Change Management Process in Section 17.
- Comprehensive organizational change management, train-the-trainer enablement, adoption tracking, and hypercare support will be delivered as part of the phased rollout.
- Any deviation from these assumptions, including scope expansion, partner onboarding changes, baseline process ownership changes, or milestone-date impacts, will require review through the Change Management Process defined in Section 17.

16.1.content:
Milestone deliverables shall be governed against the phased release plan, the Key Deliverables in Section 9, and the Commercials in Section 13. Each phase milestone shall have a defined deliverable set, due date, responsible owner, acceptance criteria, and linked billing event under the monthly fixed fee milestone model. At minimum, milestone control shall cover the manufacturing visibility target before Thanksgiving 2026, TSMC MVP and first TSMC PO by December 4, 2026, technical go-live in January 2027, Full MVP by January 25, 2027, business go-live in April 2027, hypercare completion in Q2 2027, and Phase 3 expansion and scaling through December 2027.

The milestone deliverables matrix shall be maintained as the governing traceability view for scope, acceptance, and invoicing. Any change to milestone dates, deliverable content, or acceptance basis shall be managed through Section 17.

16.2.content:
- Final inclusion or exclusion of WMS and TMS scope shall be confirmed before related design or build activities begin.
- Any international mid-stream flows remain deferred until Phase 3 and shall not be assumed in Phase 1 or Phase 2 scope.
- Any net new manufacturing collaboration or Silicon Data Hub integrations remain out of scope unless approved through change control.
- Ownership transfer points at goods receipt shall be validated during design and aligned to the approved process model.
- Any dependency on Google-owned CO/FICO activities shall be resolved in the project plan before downstream testing and cutover.

16.3.content:
- Existing Google integration frameworks shall be leveraged where feasible, with only approved delta interfaces included in scope.
- Integration scope shall be baselined during discovery across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, and E2Open, including partner connectivity with TSMC, KYEC, and SPIL.
- Any integration not included in the approved baseline shall require impact assessment and approved change control before build starts.
- Custom development shall be limited to approved functional and technical specifications tied to confirmed business requirements.
- The RICEFW and interface inventory shall be frozen at design sign-off and updated only through approved change control.
- MES, PLM, and other third-party dependency impacts shall be tracked as delivery risks and escalated through governance.

16.4.content: All scope, timeline, commercial, integration, custom code, and dependency changes shall follow the Change Management Process in Section 17. No work outside the approved scope baseline, including additional interfaces, new functional areas, or expanded regional flows, shall proceed without documented impact assessment and written approval. Approved changes shall update the applicable sections of this SOW, including Key Deliverables, Project Plan, Assumptions, Risks, and Commercials.

17.content:
Changes to scope, schedule, deliverables, staffing, integrations, commercials, or assumptions will be managed through the formal Change Request process below. No work outside the approved scope will be performed until the applicable Change Request is reviewed, approved, and reflected in the governing project baseline and, where required, this SOW.

| Step | Activity | Owner | Timeline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CR raised | Google or Bristlecone identifies a requested or required change, including the business reason and affected scope, milestone, dependency, or assumption. | Requesting Party | Within 2 business days of identifying the change |
| 2 | CR logged | The change is recorded in the project change log with a unique tracking reference and initial priority. | Bristlecone Project Manager | Within 1 business day of receipt |
| 3 | Impact assessment | Delivery, functional, integration, schedule, and commercial impact are assessed, including effect on phased milestones such as December 4, 2026, January 2027, and April 2027 commitments where applicable. | Bristlecone Project Manager with Google Project Lead and impacted workstream leads | Within 5 business days of logging |
| 4 | CR reviewed / approved | The parties review the impact assessment and approve, reject, or defer the change in writing. | Google Authorized Representative and Bristlecone Authorized Representative | Within 5 business days of impact assessment completion |
| 5 | SOW amendment / addendum | If the approved change affects scope, timeline, pricing, deliverables, or obligations, the parties execute the required SOW amendment, addendum, or written commercial approval before implementation. | Google and Bristlecone Contract Owners | Within 10 business days of approval |
| 6 | CR closure | Approved changes are incorporated into the plan and closed after implementation; rejected or deferred changes are closed with status recorded. | Bristlecone Project Manager | Within 2 business days of final disposition or implementation |

Emergency decisions needed to protect planned go-live or cutover activities may be reviewed on an expedited basis, but must still be logged and approved through the same process. Changes arising from deferred decisions, integration expansion, or scope items currently identified as out of scope will be treated as formal Change Requests.
